subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
subtype: Approach: finding an ally in the group [Action]
passage: After the temple fair, seven of them stood at the foot of the old water tower. "First one up the ladder gets a laddoo," said Suresh, rubbing his hands. Minakshi looked at the rusted rungs and her mouth went dry. Madhuri stood next to her with arms folded tight. Under her breath, Minakshi said, "Are you okay with this?" Madhuri shook her head, eyes wide. "No. Are you?" "No." Two words, and Minakshi's shoulders dropped. "We're not going up," she said, louder this time. "We'll hold the bags." Suresh groaned. "Boring!" But Madhuri did not move and neither did Minakshi, and two of the others glanced at each other and began to drift back. They ended up eating laddoos on the temple steps.

qa.q: How many friends stood at the foot of the water tower?
qa.a: Seven of them stood at the foot of the old water tower.

qa.q: How did Minakshi feel when Madhuri said 'No. Are you?'
qa.a: Minakshi felt relieved, shown by her shoulders dropping, since she was no longer alone in the doubt. 😊

qa.q: What could Minakshi do if Madhuri had said she was fine with it, and why?
qa.a: Minakshi could still say no for herself, suggest something else, and walk away, since one clear no still helps others who are unsure.

qa.q: How might Madhuri have felt before Minakshi asked?
qa.a: Madhuri was probably tense and alone with the worry, as the tightly folded arms and wide eyes suggest.

grounding: By quietly asking one friend if she is comfortable, the student finds support, and two people declining together makes it far easier to say no than standing alone.

subtopic: Facing peer pressure to do something unsafe
subtype: Approach: finding an ally in the group [Action]
passage: At the skate park in Leeds, the older kids had found a way onto the roof of the old bus depot next door, and now Callum wanted everyone up there before dark. "It's easy, there's a drainpipe." Tariq looked at the rusty pipe and the drop onto concrete. Everyone else seemed excited. Then he noticed Yuki, standing a little behind, twisting the strap of her helmet. He edged over. "You okay with this?" he asked quietly. "Not really," she whispered. "I thought I was the only one." "Me too." They looked at each other. Then Tariq said, loud enough: "We're out. Yuki and I are doing the bowl." Saying "we" felt completely different from saying "I". Callum rolled his eyes, but two more kids drifted over to the bowl too.

qa.q: What did Callum want everyone to climb onto?
qa.a: The roof of the old bus depot.

qa.q: What does Yuki twisting her helmet strap suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt nervous and uneasy about the climb.

qa.q: Why did finding Yuki make saying no easier?
qa.a: Two people declining together is harder to mock than one alone, and it showed others that refusing was possible.

qa.q: How does Callum react to the refusal?
qa.a: Callum rolls his eyes, annoyed, but can't do much as two more kids drift over to the bowl.

grounding: Shows a student quietly asking one friend if she is comfortable, and the two declining together so saying no becomes easier.

passage: At the district sports camp, after the coaches had gone to dinner, some seniors dared the juniors to jump off the five-metre diving board. Half of them couldn't swim properly. Kiran couldn't. As the chanting started, Kiran scanned the group and saw Mehak by the bench, arms wrapped tight around herself. Kiran slid next to her. "Are you okay doing this?" Mehak shook her head. "I can barely float." "Me neither. Let's just say no. Together." They stood up. "We're not jumping," Kiran said. "Neither of us." A senior scoffed, but a third junior stepped back to join them, then a fourth. Mehak went to fetch the coach from the dining hall, and five minutes later the pool gate was locked.

qa.q: How high was the diving board?
What did Mehak's arms wrapped tight around herself suggest?
qa.a: It suggested she felt scared and uneasy about the jump.

qa.q: Why did saying no together work?
qa.a: With two refusing, others felt safe to step back too, and it became much harder for the seniors to push.

qa.q: How might the seniors see the juniors refusing?
qa.a: The seniors may feel annoyed as their audience shrinks, and the coach's arrival ends the dare.

grounding: Shows a student quietly finding a friend who is also uneasy, and the two refusing together, followed by a coach locking the pool.
